decisions.reason: Define-XML ADTTE.ADT requires a nonmissing ASTDT strictly after TRTSDT, while the guide page-5 identifies the published AOCC01FL occurrence and SAP page-16 includes same-day treatment-emergent events. Probe lines 59-70 and 92-130 select that occurrence before applying the strict guard and RFENDTC conversion, so the five reported same-day differences follow the literal date rule.

Define-XML ADTTE.STARTDT names ADSL.RFSTDTC, whose ADSL section names DM.RFSTDTC, but adtte.yaml line 287 reads ADSL.TRTSDT. The complete specification does not route that derivation through RFSTDTC, so agreement of the observed dates does not supply the documented copy source.

Define-XML ADTTE.ADT explicitly requires a nonmissing event date after TRTSDT, but FIRST_DERM and HAS_EVENT in adtte.yaml lines 63-75 and 298-313 only select AOCC01FL and test AESEQ presence. The guide page-5 flag description and inclusive ADAE.TRTEMFL definition do not impose the missing strict date guard elsewhere in this path.

Define-XML ADTTE.SRCSEQ requires AESEQ when SRCDOM=ADAE and null otherwise; adtte.yaml lines 298-304 and 378-381 make SRCDOM=ADAE exactly when FIRST_DERM.AESEQ is nonmissing. The direct FIRST_DERM.AESEQ derivation at line 409 therefore already enforces both branches without an additional case expression.

The guide page-5 and Define-XML ADAE.AOCC01FL state chronological ASTDT/AESEQ ordering, but no retained section specifies placement of missing sort keys. FIRST_DERM in adtte.yaml lines 71-73 adds nulls: last for both keys on the ADT source path.

Define-XML ADAE.AOCC01FL and the guide page-5 describe ASTDT/AESEQ order but do not state a missing-key ordering rule anywhere in the retained sections. The CNSR path uses FIRST_DERM through HAS_EVENT, including the explicit nulls: last choices at adtte.yaml lines 71-73.

The guide page-5 and Define-XML ADAE.AOCC01FL document the source occurrence and ASTDT/AESEQ ordering without defining where missing keys sort. SRCSEQ reads FIRST_DERM.AESEQ, whose helper adds the undocumented nulls: last choices at adtte.yaml lines 71-73.

SAP page-10 defines end of study generally but does not state a visit-to-RFENDTC transformation or a separate ADT censoring calculation. Define-XML ADTTE.ADT names the RFENDTC conversion, which adtte.yaml line 313 supplies through the documented ADSL.RFENDT conversion, so this contextual convention does not establish a missing local ADT clause.

Define-XML ADTTE.SRCDOM names the domain actually used for ADT, but neither that section nor the guide page-5 identifies it independently when selected ADAE.ASTDT and ADSL.RFENDT coincide with published ADT. Holding published ADT fixed leaves that provenance choice incomplete, while retired probe lines 147-153 instead reuse the separately rederived strict ADT calculation and are not a claimed literal.

Define-XML ADTTE.SRCVAR names the variable actually used for ADT, but that section, ADTTE.ADT and the guide page-5 do not identify actual provenance independently when the two source dates coincide with published ADT. The documented ADSL.RFENDT conversion identifies the fallback candidate without resolving that ambiguity, and retired probe lines 154-160 reconstruct upstream ADT rather than provide a claimed independent literal.
